task:
READ-ONLY REPO-WIDE V3 MAP / NEW-FEATURE DOCUMENT AUTHORITY AUDIT. Do not modify files, commit, push, deploy, access production, read secrets, or mutate databases. Audit the current repository documentation comprehensively for anything that describes, constrains, proposes, supersedes, or historically implemented the new Galaxy Map / Babylon spatial platform or adjacent new product features. The goal is to create an implementation-ready authority map before Search/grid/clusters and the Babylon product design advance further.

SCOPE
Search the entire documentation tree plus root README.md, CHANGES.md and CLAUDE.md. Include docs/ROADMAP.md; docs/colonisation-redesign/**; docs/development/**; docs/superpowers/specs/** and plans/**; docs/research/**; docs/reference/** where relevant; docs/archive/** only when it contains feature intent that may not have been promoted elsewhere. Also identify repository tests that hard-code document wording/authorization state. Use PR #601 current migration state as an important comparison point, but do not modify it.

FEATURE TERMS / CONCEPTS TO TRACE
- Galaxy Map, map, spatial platform, Babylon, R3F/Three, renderer, semantic zoom, real-star streaming, viewport, LOD, regions, heatmap, clusters, routes, selection/picking, camera, Find Around Here, Systems Within, search-from-here, radius sync, map/Finder synchronization.
- Explore/Finder, Inspect/System Detail, Compare, saved candidates/watchlist, Planner/Plan, Review/Export.
- System Map, BodyRef/body identity, stars/bodies/rings/stations/settlements/facilities, Architect Mode / primary-port context, schematic vs authoritative placement, fidelity levels.
- Commander History, Journal, Exploration, expeditions, timeline/playback, reverse spatial queries, personal vs catalogue truth, Codex, exobiology.
- Colonisation overlays/infrastructure, Powerplay, Routes, route planning/corridors.
- CRE Digital Twin, CPE planning overlays/alternatives, planner-map interactions and mutation boundaries.
- New or deferred adjacent features: mission intelligence, mining/rings, accounts/sync/collaboration, evidence overlays, any other user-facing future capability discovered in docs.

REQUIRED CLASSIFICATION
For every materially relevant document, classify it as one of:
A. CURRENT NORMATIVE AUTHORITY — durable product/architecture/stack/validation/runtime rule that should guide new work now.
B. CURRENT BUT STALE STATUS — intended authority whose current-state/authorization/deployment wording is behind the actual migration state and needs re-baselining.
C. HISTORICAL EVIDENCE / BEHAVIOUR ORACLE — useful requirements, tests, performance findings or feature ideas that may inform V3 but must not override current authority.
D. SUPERSEDED / MISLEADING — wording that conflicts with current accepted direction and should be archived, annotated, or corrected so agents do not follow it.
E. DEFERRED FEATURE AUTHORITY — still valid future intent but not part of the current checkpoint.

CONTRADICTIONS TO CHECK EXPLICITLY
1. Stage 25 map-is-secondary-Explore-only wording versus Stage 27 One Spatial Platform and map participation across Explore -> Inspect -> Plan -> Review.
2. Stage 27A/27B 'Babylon not authorized / isolated non-product only' wording versus the actual governed #601 migration, fresh apps/web Babylon map, Explore/Finder -> map/results -> Inspect product slice and current validation work.
3. R3F/Three 'production baseline/rollback until later bakeoff' language versus the V3 hard-replacement stack decision and React/R3F retirement target. Distinguish historical production fact from current migration authority.
4. Any docs saying Finder/Inspect/product map 'come later' when those surfaces are now present on #601.
5. Any hard-coded Contabo-as-live-checkpoint assumption versus the corrected topology: Contabo's proven role is the self-hosted Codex runner host; a checkpoint there is only conditional on capacity/isolation and is not production. Production is ed-finder-prod.
6. Ratings/scoring documentation conflicts that affect Search/map: legacy Ratings v3.4 versus archetype canonical scoring, current search dependencies, CRE future direction. Do not resolve scoring semantics without evidence; identify the authority conflict.
7. Stage 26 map plans/specs, including real-star streaming/exploration/Babylon proposals, that contain valuable feature requirements but are no longer current roadmap authority.
8. Current tests that enforce obsolete documentation text and would need updating in a doc re-baseline.

FEATURE RECOVERY
Create a feature ledger of useful requirements/ideas found anywhere in the docs, even historical sources, and state whether each is already represented in current Stage 27 authority. Examples: semantic zoom; real-star viewport streaming/hysteresis/truncation; Find Around Here; radius ring; result/map hover/selection sync; cluster inspection; region layers; commander travel history/expeditions; System Map; Architect Mode/primary-port guidance; colonised infrastructure; Powerplay; routes; CPE plan overlays; CRE Digital Twin; accessible DOM equivalents. If a historical feature is NOT represented in current authority, flag it as a candidate to consciously retain or reject rather than silently losing it.

SEARCH / GRID / CLUSTER IMPLICATIONS
Extract every current or historical feature requirement that should influence the Search/grid/cluster data architecture now: viewport-driven queries, arbitrary radius, local/regional/wide semantic zoom, bounded result counts, cluster membership, multi-economy search, map-selected reference points, route corridors, personal-history overlays, etc. Do not design the database itself in this audit; give requirements that the separate search-spatial audit should satisfy.

OUTPUT
Return:
- exact audited SHA and whether main or #601-specific docs were inspected;
- authority hierarchy and recommended 'read this first' order;
- exhaustive relevant-document table with classification and one-line disposition;
- contradiction/staleness register ranked Critical/High/Medium/Low;
- feature ledger with source docs and current authority status;
- Search/grid/cluster requirement extraction;
- exact docs that should be edited in the first re-baseline pass and exact historical docs that should only receive status banners/links rather than rewrites;
- tests that hard-code stale wording and would need coordinated updates;
- proposed small, bounded doc re-baseline packet (no implementation) that can run after this audit.

Explicitly confirm no files or external environments were changed.
